vocab.definition: a salt that dissolves in water.
extra base added to use up all the acid.
evaporates water to leave salt crystals.

misconceptions.wrong: Add just enough base to the acid.
misconceptions.right: Add base in EXCESS so all the acid reacts.

misconceptions.wrong: Boil the solution dry to get crystals.
misconceptions.right: Evaporate gently and let it crystallise.
Filter to remove the unreacted excess solid.

infoPanels.title: METHOD (insoluble base)
workedSteps: Warm the acid in a beaker.
!Add the base (e.g. copper oxide) until in excess.
Heat the filtrate to the point of crystallisation.

questions.text: Explain why the base is added in excess. [2 marks]
Name the technique used to remove the unreacted base. [1 mark]
Describe how to obtain dry crystals from the salt solution. [3 marks]
Name the acid and base needed to make copper sulfate. [2 marks]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: Add the base in ______, then ______ off the unreacted solid.

questions.text: Explain why the solution is not heated strongly to dryness. [1 mark]

footer.tip: Excess base → filter → crystallise. Excess ensures all acid is neutralised.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why does slow crystallisation give larger, purer crystals?
